subject.title: All LLM API calls time out simultaneously despite APIs being reachable (multi-agent concurrency issue)

question: Should OpenClaw decouple Telegram runner sink concurrency from agents.defaults.maxConcurrent for multi-agent Telegram deployments, or keep the shared concurrency model and document/tune supported operator settings?
rationale: The remaining code-backed gap changes how channel ingress competes with agent turn concurrency, which affects delivery behavior and operator expectations beyond a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Require live current-main trace first
options.body: Capture a four-agent Telegram/provider trace before changing concurrency semantics, then decide whether ingress starvation is still present.

options.title: Decouple Telegram ingress concurrency
options.body: Add a Telegram-owned concurrency policy or derived default with live Telegram proof and regression coverage for concurrent agent load.

options.title: Keep shared concurrency
options.body: Leave sink concurrency tied to agent maxConcurrent and improve diagnostics or docs around provider timeout and process-level tuning.

recommendation.title: Require live current-main trace first
recommendation.body: Capture a four-agent Telegram/provider trace before changing concurrency semantics, then decide whether ingress starvation is still present.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-main ownership signal is the Telegram monitor concurrency line plus adjacent recent Telegram monitor history.
